theory.intro: **Network flow analysis** uses the minimum cut to determine how changes to edge capacities affect maximum flow.
facts: Maximum flow equals the capacity of the minimum cut.
Increasing an edge outside a minimum cut leaves that cut unchanged, so it cannot increase maximum flow.
A successful upgrade must increase every cut that restricts the target flow. An edge may belong to more than one cut.
If an edge's reduced capacity still allows its flow in an existing maximum-flow assignment, maximum flow is unchanged.
Reducing an edge below its flow in a maximum-flow assignment may require rerouting. Recalculate the restrictive cuts before deciding whether maximum flow decreases.
steps: Determine the minimum cut and maximum flow of the network
Compare the maximum flow to the target demand when planning an upgrade
Identify which edges belong to the minimum cut bottleneck
Evaluate the impact of changing specific edge capacities on the minimum cut

workedExamples.solution_text:
The four source–sink cut capacities are:
$\begin{aligned}SA+SB&=60+40=100\\AT+AB+SB&=50+20+40=110\\AT+BT&=50+70=120\\SA+BT&=60+70=130\end{aligned}$
The minimum cut gives maximum flow $100\text{ kL/h}$, which is $15\text{ kL/h}$ below demand.
Both cuts below $115\text{ kL/h}$ contain $SB$. Increase $SB$ by $15\text{ kL/h}$, from $40$ to $55\text{ kL/h}$.
The four cut capacities become $115$, $125$, $120$ and $130\text{ kL/h}$. The new maximum flow is $115\text{ kL/h}$, so demand is met.

workedExamples.question_text:
A water network has minimum cut $C_1$ containing pipes with capacities $42$ and $28\text{ L/s}$. Its second-smallest cut, $C_2$, has capacity $79\text{ L/s}$ and contains neither pipe. Every other cut has capacity at least $79\text{ L/s}$.
The first pipe is enlarged from $42$ to $57\text{ L/s}$. Find the new maximum flow. Does it meet demand of $82\text{ L/s}$?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Originally, $C_1$ has capacity $42+28=70\text{ L/s}$.
After the upgrade, its capacity is $57+28=85\text{ L/s}$.
Cut $C_2$ remains at $79\text{ L/s}$, and every other cut retains capacity at least $79\text{ L/s}$.
The new maximum flow is $79\text{ L/s}$. Demand is not met; the shortfall is $82-79=3\text{ L/s}$.

workedExamples.question_text:
A road network has a unique minimum cut consisting of two roads with capacities $80$ and $55\text{ vehicles/min}$. Roadworks reduce the first road's capacity to $62\text{ vehicles/min}$.
Find the new maximum flow and decide whether demand of $120\text{ vehicles/min}$ can still be met.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The original maximum flow is $80+55=135\text{ vehicles/min}$.
The original minimum cut now has capacity $62+55=117\text{ vehicles/min}$.
Every other cut loses at most $18\text{ vehicles/min}$ and originally had capacity greater than $135\text{ vehicles/min}$, so this cut remains minimum.
The new maximum flow is $117\text{ vehicles/min}$. Demand is not met; the shortfall is $120-117=3\text{ vehicles/min}$.

workedExamples.question_text:
A pipe network has maximum flow $72\text{ L/s}$. In one maximum-flow assignment, pipe $XY$ has capacity $32\text{ L/s}$ but carries only $21\text{ L/s}$.
Maintenance reduces its capacity to $25\text{ L/s}$. Determine the new maximum flow and whether demand of $70\text{ L/s}$ can still be met.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The reduced capacity still permits the assigned flow because $25>21$.
The same maximum-flow assignment remains feasible. Reducing a capacity cannot increase maximum flow, so maximum flow remains $72\text{ L/s}$.
Demand of $70\text{ L/s}$ is still met, with $2\text{ L/s}$ spare capacity.

workedExamples.question_text:
A distribution network has maximum flow $160\text{ tonnes/day}$. Its unique minimum cut contains edge $E_1$ but excludes edge $E_2$. Every other cut has capacity at least $195\text{ tonnes/day}$.
Maintenance reduces $E_1$ by $18\text{ tonnes/day}$ and $E_2$ by $12\text{ tonnes/day}$. Both resulting capacities are non-negative. In an original maximum-flow assignment, $E_2$ had $16\text{ tonnes/day}$ of unused capacity.
Find the resulting maximum flow and decide whether demand of $145\text{ tonnes/day}$ is met.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The original minimum cut contains only $E_1$ of the two changed edges. Its new capacity is $160-18=142\text{ tonnes/day}$.
Any other cut loses at most $18+12=30\text{ tonnes/day}$, leaving capacity at least $195-30=165\text{ tonnes/day}$.
The new minimum cut therefore has capacity $142\text{ tonnes/day}$, giving maximum flow $142\text{ tonnes/day}$.
Demand is not met; the shortfall is $145-142=3\text{ tonnes/day}$.
The original unused capacity on $E_2$ alone does not establish the result after both reductions.

foundation.question_text:
A network has source $S$ and sink $T$.
The unique minimum cut consists of edges $SA (20)$ and $SB (15)$ with a capacity of $35$.
Every other cut has capacity at least $40$.
Edge $BC$ has capacity $8$ (the smallest in the network), but is not part of the minimum cut.
Which edge could be upgraded, and by how much, to increase the maximum flow to $36$?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Identify which edges belong to the minimum cut bottleneck**
The minimum cut consists of edges $SA$ and $SB$.
Increase either $SA$ or $SB$ by $1$.
This raises the cut capacity to $36$, while every other cut still has capacity at least $40$.
The new maximum flow is $36$.

foundation.question_text:
A distribution network has a maximum flow of $50\text{ tonnes/day}$.
In a maximum-flow assignment, edge $XY$ has a capacity of $20\text{ tonnes/day}$ but carries only $12\text{ tonnes/day}$ of flow.
If maintenance reduces the capacity of edge $XY$ to $15\text{ tonnes/day}$, what is the effect on the maximum flow of the network?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Evaluate the impact of changing specific edge capacities on the minimum cut**
In the maximum-flow assignment, edge $XY$ carries $12\text{ tonnes/day}$.
The reduced capacity ($15\text{ tonnes/day}$) still allows this flow.
The existing assignment remains possible, and reducing a capacity cannot increase maximum flow.
The overall maximum flow remains $50\text{ tonnes/day}$ (unchanged).

foundation.question_text:
A network has a minimum cut $C_1$ with capacity $60$ across edges $SA (35)$ and $SB (25)$.
The next smallest cut $C_2$ has capacity $68$ and does not contain $SA$.
If pipe $SA$ is enlarged so its capacity increases by $10$ (to $45$), what is the new maximum flow of the network?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Evaluate the impact of changing specific edge capacities on the minimum cut**
New capacity of cut $C_1 = 45 + 25 = 70$
Capacity of cut $C_2 = 68$, unchanged because it does not contain $SA$.
Every other cut originally had capacity at least $68$, and the upgrade cannot reduce its capacity.
Since $68 < 70$, cut $C_2$ is now a minimum cut.
$\text{New maximum flow} = 68$

foundation.question_text:
A pipeline network currently has a maximum flow of $85\text{ L/s}$.
Target demand is $100\text{ L/s}$.
The minimum cut consists of pipes $SA (50)$ and $SB (35)$, and no other cut has capacity less than $105\text{ L/s}$.
By how much must pipe $SA$ or $SB$ be increased to achieve the target demand?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Compare the maximum flow to the target demand when planning an upgrade**
$\text{Required increase} = \text{Target demand} - \text{Current max flow}$
$= 100 - 85$
$= 15\text{ L/s}$
Increase pipe $SA$ or $SB$ by $15\text{ L/s}$.

development.solution_text:
1. **Evaluate the impact of changing specific edge capacities on the minimum cut**
Original cuts:
Source cut $\{SA, SB\} = 40 + 30 = 70$ (minimum cut)
Cut $\{AT, AB, SB\} = 35 + 10 + 30 = 75$
Sink cut $\{AT, BT\} = 35 + 45 = 80$
After upgrading $SA$ to $55$:
New source cut $\{SA, SB\} = 55 + 30 = 85$
Cut $\{AT, AB, SB\} = 35 + 10 + 30 = 75$ is now the new minimum cut.
$\text{New maximum flow} = 75$

development.question_text:
A road network has maximum flow of $120\text{ vehicles/min}$.
The unique minimum cut consists of road segments $R_1 (70)$ and $R_2 (50)$.
During roadworks, segment $R_1$ is reduced from $70$ to $45\text{ vehicles/min}$.
Calculate the new maximum flow and the reduction in network capacity.
development.solution_text:
1. **Evaluate the impact of changing specific edge capacities on the minimum cut**
$\text{New minimum cut capacity} = 45 + 50$
$= 95\text{ vehicles/min}$
$\text{Capacity reduction} = 120 - 95$
$= 25\text{ vehicles/min}$
$\text{New maximum flow} = 95\text{ vehicles/min}$

development.question_text:
A wildlife park path network has capacities $SA = 25, SB = 20, AC = 18, BC = 12, BD = 15, CD = 8, CT = 20, DT = 22$. Each edge is directed from its first named vertex to its second.
Park management wants to increase maximum visitor flow from $38$ to $39\text{ visitors/hour}$.
Which single path could be widened, and by how much?
development.solution_text:
1. **Identify which edges belong to the minimum cut bottleneck**
The minimum cut is $\{SB, AC\}$, with capacity $20 + 18 = 38\text{ visitors/hour}$.
Increase $AC$ from $18$ to $19\text{ visitors/hour}$.
The cut capacity becomes $20 + 19 = 39\text{ visitors/hour}$.
This flow is possible with edge flows $SA = 19, SB = 20, AC = 19, BC = 5, BD = 15, CD = 4, CT = 20, DT = 19$.
Thus widening $AC$ by $1\text{ visitor/hour}$ achieves the target. Increasing $SB$ by $1\text{ visitor/hour}$ is also suitable.

development.question_text:
A stormwater drainage network has source $S$, sink $T$ and intermediate vertices $A$ and $B$.
Its pipe capacities are $SA = 90, SB = 60, AT = 80, BT = 100, AB = 20$, all in $\text{kL/h}$. Each pipe is directed from its first named vertex to its second.
Which single pipe could be increased in capacity, and by how much, so that the overall maximum flow will be $175\text{ kL/h}$?
development.solution_text:
1. **Identify which edges belong to the minimum cut bottleneck**
The four cut capacities are $SA + SB = 150$, $AT + AB + SB = 160$, $AT + BT = 180$ and $SA + BT = 190$, all in $\text{kL/h}$.
The current maximum flow is $150\text{ kL/h}$.
Pipe $SB$ belongs to both cuts below the target of $175\text{ kL/h}$.
Increase $SB$ by $175 - 150 = 25\text{ kL/h}$, from $60$ to $85\text{ kL/h}$.
The four cut capacities become $175$, $185$, $180$ and $190\text{ kL/h}$.
The new minimum cut has capacity $175\text{ kL/h}$, so this single-pipe upgrade achieves the target.

development.question_text:
A water network has edge capacities: $SP = 80, SQ = 60, PQ = 20, PT = 70, QT = 65$.
The current minimum cut is $\{PT, QT\}$ with capacity $70 + 65 = 135$.
Pipe $PT$ is enlarged from $70$ to $90$.
Find the new maximum flow from $S$ to $T$.
development.solution_text:
1. **Evaluate the impact of changing specific edge capacities on the minimum cut**
New capacity of sink cut $\{PT, QT\} = 90 + 65 = 155$
Source cut $\{SP, SQ\} = 80 + 60 = 140$
Cut $\{PT, PQ, SQ\} = 90 + 20 + 60 = 170$
Since $140 < 155$, source cut $\{SP, SQ\}$ is now the new minimum cut.
$\text{New maximum flow} = 140$

development.question_text:
In a communication network with maximum throughput $95\text{ Gbps}$, optical link $BC$ has capacity $50\text{ Gbps}$ and carries $30\text{ Gbps}$ in a maximum-flow assignment.
A technical fault reduces link $BC$'s capacity to $38\text{ Gbps}$.
Determine the new maximum throughput of the network.
development.solution_text:
1. **Evaluate the impact of changing specific edge capacities on the minimum cut**
Utilised flow through link $BC$ in the maximum-flow assignment is $30\text{ Gbps}$.
The reduced capacity of $38\text{ Gbps}$ still allows that flow ($38 > 30$).
The existing maximum-flow assignment remains possible, and reducing capacity cannot increase throughput.
The network throughput remains $95\text{ Gbps}$.

mastery.question_text:
A fuel distribution network has source $S$, sink $T$ and intermediate vertices $A$ and $B$.
Its pipe capacities are $SA = 240, SB = 180, AT = 210, BT = 270, AB = 60$, all in $\text{kL/day}$. Each pipe is directed from its first named vertex to its second.
Which single pipe could be increased in capacity, and by how much, so that the overall maximum flow will be $465\text{ kL/day}$?
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Identify which edges belong to the minimum cut bottleneck**
The four cut capacities are $SA + SB = 420$, $AT + AB + SB = 450$, $AT + BT = 480$ and $SA + BT = 510$, all in $\text{kL/day}$.
The current maximum flow is $420\text{ kL/day}$.
Pipe $SB$ belongs to both cuts below the target of $465\text{ kL/day}$.
Increase $SB$ by $465 - 420 = 45\text{ kL/day}$, from $180$ to $225\text{ kL/day}$.
The four cut capacities become $465$, $495$, $480$ and $510\text{ kL/day}$.
The new minimum cut has capacity $465\text{ kL/day}$, so this single-pipe upgrade achieves the target.

mastery.question_text:
A network has three candidate cuts: $C_1 = 200, C_2 = 215, C_3 = 230$.
Two pipes on Cut $C_1$ are increased by $20$ and $10$ respectively.
Neither upgraded pipe belongs to $C_2$ or $C_3$. Every other cut has capacity at least $230$ before the upgrades.
Calculate the new maximum flow and identify which cut is the new bottleneck.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Evaluate the impact of changing specific edge capacities on the minimum cut**
New $\text{Capacity}(C_1) = 200 + 20 + 10 = 230$
$\text{Capacity}(C_2) = 215$
$\text{Capacity}(C_3) = 230$
Neither competing cut contains an upgraded pipe, so both stay unchanged. All other cuts retain capacity at least $230$.
Cut $C_2$ is the new minimum cut.
$\text{New maximum flow} = 215$

mastery.question_text:
A network with maximum flow $150$ has two edges undergoing maintenance simultaneously: edge $E_1$ (on the unique minimum cut, reduced by $20$) and edge $E_2$ (with $15$ slack capacity in an original maximum-flow assignment, reduced by $10$).
The minimum cut does not contain $E_2$, and every other cut has capacity at least $180$ before maintenance. Both reduced edge capacities remain non-negative.
Calculate the resulting maximum flow of the network.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Evaluate the impact of changing specific edge capacities on the minimum cut**
The original minimum cut contains $E_1$ but not $E_2$, so its new capacity is $150 - 20 = 130$.
Any other cut loses at most $20 + 10 = 30$, leaving capacity at least $180 - 30 = 150$.
The new minimum cut therefore has capacity $130$.
$\text{New maximum flow} = 130$
The original slack on $E_2$ alone would not establish the result after both changes.
